source.reads: ts, first_opened_ts, elapsed_s and session_id of each audit save record, the cell_id prefix (control vs primary) and the session log's start/end lines; no label, draft field, note or span is used
source.writes: aggregates only; no cell id, session id, label, note or span

method.elapsed_s_formula: elapsed_s = round(t_save - t_open, 1). t_save is time.time() on the server, read inside Store.save (label_assist.py @ f855e62, L383). t_open is datetime.fromisoformat(first_opened).timestamp(), where first_opened is the string new Date().toISOString() that the rater's browser took when the row page loaded (L704) and posted with the save (L787): the client clock. A negative result is stored as null (L400-401); a non-empty first_opened that does not parse also gives null, with no fallback to the previous-save interval (L391-397). With d = client clock - server clock, elapsed_s = dwell - d: a client clock ahead of the server shrinks dwell (null once d exceeds the dwell), one behind it inflates dwell. The audit ts is the server wall clock at audit write, truncated to whole seconds (now_iso, L130 and L416); first_opened_ts is the raw client string. The server never records when a row was served.
method.delta: delta = ts(k) - ts(k-1) for consecutive saves of one session, ordered by (ts, file order). The next row page loads right after a save, so delta = dwell + page-load latency (+-1 s from the whole-second ts): a server-clock upper bound on dwell. The first save of a session has no delta. Sub-second variant: delta_p = t(k) - t(k-1) with t = first_opened + elapsed_s, which is the server save time because the client clock cancels (resolution 0.1 s, the rounding of elapsed_s).
method.skew_estimator: s = first_opened(k) - t(k-1): the client's page-load stamp of row k minus the server's save time of the previous row, t as above. s = d + tau with d = client clock - server clock and tau >= 0 the latency from the previous save to the page script of the next row, so a constant skew d shifts every s by d. D = delta - elapsed_s equals s up to the whole-second ts quantization. client_lead_upper_bound_s = min(s) + 0.05 s (d <= s - tau <= s, plus the rounding of elapsed_s).
method.g7_total_dwell_rule: a cell's total dwell is the sum of elapsed_s over all its saves (analyze_holdout._g7, condition c); it is fast when under 20 s; G7 needs fewer than 3% fast primary cells (PREREG L349)

bootstrap.draw: int(random.Random(seed).random() * n) for each of n draws with replacement; a fresh generator per interval
bootstrap.interval: percentile: sorted resampled medians at index B*25//1000 and B*975//1000

method.quantiles: linear interpolation between order statistics (numpy default)

formula_check.quantity: ts - (first_opened + elapsed_s); expected in [-1.05, +0.15] s: ts is the server clock truncated to whole seconds and written a few ms after the save time, elapsed_s is rounded to 0.1 s

delta_upper_bound_check.reading: 0 means every row page loaded after the previous save, so delta bounds the dwell from above

break_even_client_lead.meaning: uniform amount (s) added to every elapsed_s, i.e. a client clock ahead of the server by this much, for fewer than 3% of primary cells to stay under 20 s

caveats: delta bounds a row's dwell from above only if the row page loaded after the previous save; delta_upper_bound_check counts the saves with elapsed_s > delta + 1 s.
Whole-second delta has +-1 s quantization (the audit ts is truncated to seconds). The sub-second delta and the skew estimator carry the 0.1 s rounding of elapsed_s.

A client clock behind the server inflates elapsed_s, the direction that would flatter G7; only a client clock ahead of the server could make the dwell look too short, and client_lead_upper_bound_s bounds that lead.
Idle-gap rows (s above 5 s: the next row loaded more than 5 s after the previous save) are not skew. They stay in the all-rows statistics and are left out of the excluding_idle_gaps variants.
Bootstrap intervals are percentile intervals over rows treated as independent; within-session correlation is ignored, so they are descriptive.
Every cell was saved once, so a cell's total dwell (the registered G7 basis, the sum of elapsed_s over its saves) equals that save's value; the script stops if a cell has more than one save.
A primary cell with no within-session predecessor has no delta: it is left out of the delta-basis share (n_with_value) and counted in share_bounds_all_primary_cells.
The check validates the timing measurement only. It says nothing about rater effort, and the labels are AH (AI-drafted, human-revised); see annotation_locked/LOCK_2026-10-09.md.
